incident-bot: PAGE: High error rate on /v1/session/create from multiple edge clusters — 5xx spike and embedding queue latency surge. Pager: @sam (oncall)

sam (oncall): I'm on. Quick glance at logs: sustained fanout from many /24s in EU/APAC, UA patterns: python-requests and curl. 95th latency ~2.3s, errors ~8%. Suspect coordinated scraper/session probe.

maria-support: getting tickets from customers c-834 and c-902 complaining about timeouts and failed batch uploads. Adding them to impacted list.

alex-infra: I can push a WAF tarpit rule to edge (match UA + ASN ranges) and add ip-rate limits. Will need a couple minutes.

jess-sre: +1. Also recommend disabling embeddings batch endpoint temporarily and putting a soft per-account quota to stop noisy tenants.

sam (oncall): Plan of action: 1) Deploy WAF tarpit rule for matching UA/ASN 2) Add per-IP rate-slice on /v1/session/create (5 req/min) 3) Soft per-account session quota 100/min with 429 backoff 4) Disable embeddings-batch temporarily 5) Route huge requests to low-cost fallback model. Execute and monitor.

alex-infra: Pushing WAF rule now. Command: ```edge-wafctl push --rule "match: ua:(python-requests|curl); action:tarpit; scope: eu,apac" --ttl 15m```

alex-infra: WAF rule r-98321 deployed to EU/APAC edges. Starting to observe fewer simultaneous upstream connections from the offending clusters.

jess-sre: I disabled embeddings-batch endpoint: /admin/features/embeddings-batch -> OFF. Also applied per-account soft quota: `quotactl set --scope account --limit sessions-per-minute=100 --behavior soft-429`

zach-eng: Paused public async batch ingestion to reduce KV cache thrash: `/admin/batches -> paused` (cmd executed).

maria-support: Support notified impacted customers with a short status note and workaround (retry with exponential backoff). Impacted list so far: c-834, c-902, c-771. CS to open dedicated follow-ups.

jess-sre: Added rate-slice rule: ```edgectl rate-slice add --path "/v1/session/create" --ip-rate 5/m --scope temp-scraper --mode enforce``` Rule id returned: rs-4420.

sam (oncall): Also put a routing fallback: token-count > 10k -> route to small-model instance to avoid long-running KV/cache pressure. Jess, can you apply?

jess-sre: Done. Routing rule applied: heavy->gpt-small-latency.

alex-infra: Metrics update: errors dropped from 8% -> 1.2% within 8 minutes of WAF + rate-slice. Connection fanout reduced ~6x.

maria-support: Customers reporting partial recovery; some long-running batches still delayed. We're collecting logs for c-834 and c-902 to provide postmortem context.

sam (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing this to @jess for next 2h of watch. Summary for handoff: mitigations applied = WAF tarpit (r-98321), rate-slice (rs-4420), embeddings-batch disabled, per-account soft quotas, routing fallback. Current state: traffic stabilized but some delayed processing for affected customers. Next steps for oncall: keep WAF/rate-slice active, monitor error rate and tail latencies, coordinate with support for customer updates, and prepare to re-enable batches only after 50% sustained reduction in backend latencies.

jess-sre: Acknowledged. I'll continue to monitor and escalate if we see a retrigger. I'll also open the incident ticket in the tracker with mitigation steps and tags (abuse, waf, rate-slicing, customer-impact).

incident-bot: Incident status updated -> severity: sev2 (mitigated) ; monitoring in progress. Pager cleared for initial oncall.

jess-sre: leaving note: If we see new UA variants, we'll expand WAF match and consider geo-based hard blocks for specific ASNs. If customers require SLA exceptions, route to support for a manual quota bump and audit.

maria-support: filing post-incident customer comms draft and will loop in legal if any sensitive data was affected.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (auto) — leave open if new symptoms appear.
